title: Deterministic exemplar fabric for inference latency histograms
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Prometheus histogram buckets and OTLP/trace spans are drifting for high-volume inference routes. We lack deterministic exemplar selection and synthesis when we bridge OTLP histograms into Prometheus, which makes tail-latency SLO debugging noisy and non-reproducible. This ticket introduces a deterministic "exemplar fabric": a lightweight runtime component that attaches stable, trace-linked exemplars to Prometheus-compatible latency histograms synthesized from OTLP metrics and exemplars.

Goals:
- Produce stable exemplar attachments for bucketed latency metrics so a specific percentile drop or spike can be traced back to a consistent span/sample.
- Work with both OTLP histograms and raw per-request metrics (prefix/KV cache hits) to synthesize Prometheus exposition with exemplars.
- Keep CPU/memory overhead low at high QPS (target <0.8% CPU for 32-core serving node at 50k rps).
- Provide a migration path for existing dashboards and attribution pipelines without disrupting SLIs.

Approach:
1) Deterministic exemplar selection: compute a stable fingerprint from request routing metadata (customer_id, model, route, request_hash) combined with a time-window salt. Use a bounded reservoir with deterministic replacement (e.g., keyed xor-shift + consistent hashing) so the same request maps to the same exemplar bucket across restarts within the window.
2) OTLP->Prometheus adapter: implement a streaming adapter that consumes OTLP histogram aggregations and span exemplars, emits Prometheus histograms with exemplar labels (trace_id, span_id, route, model_version) and preserves count/sum invariants. The adapter will also synthesize exemplars for cases where OTLP lacks them by selecting deterministic representative spans from recent trace buffers.
3) Backpressure & memory guards: use fixed-size ring buffers, evict oldest on pressure, and expose internal metrics for drop counts and exemplar collision rates.
4) Rollout plan: staged canary in eu-west-1 on dedicated capacity pools with mirrored pipeline to avoid impacting user SLOs.

Why this is different from prior work: existing tickets focused on ingestion, downsampling, and schema harmonization. This work focuses specifically on stable linkage between bucketed metrics and traces (exemplars) and on deterministic behavior to aid reproducible incident debugging and evaluation of tail-latency regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter emits Prometheus histogram exposition that passes Prometheus histogram invariants (count, sum) for synthetic OTLP input
Exemplars attached contain trace_id and span_id and resolve to a span in the tracing backend > 99% of the time for canary traffic
Deterministic sampling: re-running the same input feed within the same time window yields identical exemplar selection (modulo allowed salt rotation)
CPU overhead measured on a 32-core node at 50k rps < 1% (end-to-end for the adapter process), memory bounded with no OOMs observed during 48h stress test
Migration docs and a runbook exist describing how to switch dashboards from current metrics to adapter-backed metrics and how to rollback
Canary rollout for eu-west-1 completes without any customer-facing SLO violations and with exemplar resolution telemetry showing expected rates
tasks: Design deterministic fingerprint and reservoir algorithm (docs + pseudocode)
Implement OTLP histogram consumer and exemplar synthesizer in metrics-bridge service
Add bounded trace buffer and deterministic selection primitives
Expose internal metrics: exemplar_drop_count, exemplar_collision_rate, exemplar_emit_latency
Write unit and integration tests for invariants and determinism
Run 48h stress test with synthetic replay workload at 50k rps and collect perf data
Create migration guide and dashboard updates for latency/exemplar panels
